chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from the one who mentioned it, from Zurara, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is nothing which a man leaves behind which is more difficult upon him than the silent wealth; how should he deal with it?' He said: 'He should place it in the wall, meaning in the garden or the house.'

key_terms.الْمَالِ الصَّامِتِ: Silent wealth (gold and silver held in reserve)
key_terms.يَجْعَلُهُ فِي الْحَائِطِ: Placing it in the wall (burying it)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on managing gold and silver (silent wealth) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies 'silent wealth' (al-mal al-samit)—typically referring to gold and silver hoarded without circulation or investment—as a heavy burden on the owner. He advises investing it in real estate, such as a garden or house, to transform static assets into productive property. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on activating capital through tangible assets to avoid the spiritual and economic stagnation of hoarding.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from the one who mentioned it, from Zurara who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘There is nothing which the man leaves behind which is more difficult upon him than the silent wealth (gold and silver), how he should deal with it. Make it to be in the wall, meaning (bury it) in the garden, or the house?’
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from the one whom he has mentioned (in his book) from Zurarah who has said

the following: “I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, saying, The most difficult to property to protect is of the silent kind (gold and silver).’ I then asked, ‘What should one do about it?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘One should keep them inside walls, a garden or a house.’”
